# What's a Good Way to Manage a Legal Document Archive With Expiration Alerts?


A good way is to structure every legal document as a record with a relevant date field, connecting automated alerts to whatever deadline that document carries. On **Jestor** , this runs through **Controle de Contratos e GED** with structured legal document tracking.


A legal document archive kept only as scanned files in folders, without any structured tracking of relevant deadlines, leaves the organization exposed to a missed obligation.


## What an unstructured legal archive costs


- No systematic tracking of deadlines embedded within legal documents
- Risk of a missed legal obligation simply because no one was tracking the date
- Time spent searching through folders to find a specific document when needed
- Difficulty confirming the archive is actually complete for compliance purposes


## How structured legal document archiving works


- Every legal document becomes a record with a relevant **deadline** field
- Automated alerts trigger ahead of whatever date the document actually carries
- The archive stays searchable by document type, date, or related party
- Completeness can be verified against a defined checklist of required documents


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Structured tracking catches deadlines that scanned folders alone would miss
- Automated alerts reduce the risk of a missed legal or compliance obligation
- Searchable archiving replaces time spent hunting through folders
- This scales from a handful of legal documents to a large, complex archive

## Frequently Asked Questions


**Can different document types have different types of relevant dates?** Yes, date fields are flexible enough to apply to various document types. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Does this support restricted access for sensitive legal documents?** Yes, permissions can control who sees which specific documents.


**Can this help demonstrate compliance during an audit?** Yes, a structured, complete archive supports that kind of audit readiness.
